Cliff Sosin on the limits of intelligence:

"Superintelligence arrived. You probably didn't notice, because it turned out to be kind of incremental.

I think we overrated intelligence, or misread what it is. 

We hold a thin scatter of facts about the world, and intelligence or reasoning is whatever fills the space between them.

Where the space between the facts behaves well, this is close to godlike. Most of what matters doesn't behave like that. 

The universe is mostly the emergent behavior of complex systems. Stir cream into coffee. Watch a storm build out of nothing but atmospheric temperature differences and water vapor. 

You have to run the thing.

The takeoff story assumed the limit was thinking. It isn't. The limit is contact with reality. 

A smarter reasoner fills the gaps between known facts in simple areas faster and better, but it doesn’t produce new facts.

An AI will hand you a genuinely clever design for a jet turbine blade. It might be far more likely to work than anything your engineers came up with. 

It'll still probably fail, because that’s the base rate at the edge of what anyone knows. The only way to find out is to build the blade and try to break it.

That's the real limit on learning, and it doesn't care how smart you are. Coming up with ideas was never the hard part. The hard part is how fast reality answers them.

Most problems can't be worked out at a desk by thinking. Those stay bound by how fast we can build the thing and see if it holds, and that clock barely moves."

From his essay "Maybe Intelligence Ain't All That." He walks through it here.

Should you be on Reddit to drive LLM recommendations?

One of Discuss GTM’s chat members shared an unreviewed preprint study I just finished reading. It looks at whether Reddit shapes which brands AI tools recommend – even when the tools don’t cite Reddit.

Sample and methodology:

The author pulled 12K posts and 100K+ comments from 60 subreddits via Reddit’s API.

Brand mentions were scored by upvotes, placement (title, body, comment), and comment depth.

Those scores were then ranked against brand recommendations from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini across 50 product queries, each asked three times. The correlation analysis spans 12 consumer categories.

A second test compared Reddit citations in 60 API calls (15 queries) vs. 100 web UI queries per platform, collected via browser automation in February 2026.

Key findings:

• Reddit brand rankings and AI brand rankings lined up fairly strongly.
• Web UIs cited Reddit in 44% of queries on Google AI Mode, 20% on Perplexity, and 17% on ChatGPT.
• APIs returned 0% Reddit citations on every platform.
• Opinion and comparison queries pulled in Reddit most often: 70.8% on Google AI Mode and 45.8% on Perplexity.
• Claude cited Reddit zero times in both channels, but it cited any source in only 19% of web UI queries.

Now, how I read it.

Reddit may influence LLM recommendations even when it’s not cited.

The big implication: citation tracking alone may underestimate Reddit’s role. If brand rankings on Reddit correlate with brand recommendations from LLMs, Reddit may function as a background reputation / consensus layer – not just a direct source.

Remember my post about fan-out queries? Here’s the answer for getting into an LLM’s pre-search association brain.

So “being cited” and “shaping the answer” are two different things.

Reddit also seems especially relevant for high-consideration / opinion-heavy queries. So if you’re in a very competitive field and switching costs are high—yeah, you have to think about building a presence on Reddit.

Shilling is also not the answer.

Engagement quality > raw mention volume.

Because the Reddit score included upvotes, title/body placement, and comment depth, the implied signal is a brand showing up in substantive, highly engaged discussions.

Reddit = reputation channel.

I definitely need to research more guerrilla tactics on Reddit. For now, I’m just passively growing karma—but I’m not sure how to inject brand discussions without it becoming shilling / spam.

Feel free to share your ideas.

PS: This study is an unreviewed preprint from a consultancy with a stake in GEO advice, and it’s co-written with Claude folks.

The author pulled 12K posts and 100K+ comments from 60 subreddits via Reddit’s API.

Brand mentions were scored by upvotes, placement (title, body, comment), and comment depth.

Those scores were then ranked against brand recommendations from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini across 50 product queries, each asked three times. The correlation analysis spans 12 consumer categories.

A second test compared Reddit citations in 60 API calls (15 queries) vs. 100 web UI queries per platform, collected via browser automation in February 2026.

Key findings:

• Reddit brand rankings and AI brand rankings lined up fairly strongly.
• Web UIs cited Reddit in 44% of queries on Google AI Mode, 20% on Perplexity, and 17% on ChatGPT.
• APIs returned 0% Reddit citations on every platform.
• Opinion and comparison queries pulled in Reddit most often: 70.8% on Google AI Mode and 45.8% on Perplexity.
• Claude cited Reddit zero times in both channels, but it cited any source in only 19% of web UI queries.

Now, how I read it.

Reddit may influence LLM recommendations even when it’s not cited.

The big implication: citation tracking alone may underestimate Reddit’s role. If brand rankings on Reddit correlate with brand recommendations from LLMs, Reddit may function as a background reputation / consensus layer – not just a direct source.

Remember my post about fan-out queries? Here’s the answer for getting into an LLM’s pre-search association brain.

So “being cited” and “shaping the answer” are two different things.

Reddit also seems especially relevant for high-consideration / opinion-heavy queries. So if you’re in a very competitive field and switching costs are high—yeah, you have to think about building a presence on Reddit.

Shilling is also not the answer.

Engagement quality > raw mention volume.

Because the Reddit score included upvotes, title/body placement, and comment depth, the implied signal is a brand showing up in substantive, highly engaged discussions.

Reddit = reputation channel.

I definitely need to research more guerrilla tactics on Reddit. For now, I’m just passively growing karma—but I’m not sure how to inject brand discussions without it becoming shilling / spam.

Feel free to share your ideas.

PS: This study is an unreviewed preprint from a consultancy with a stake in GEO advice, and it’s co-written with Claude folks.

I don’t buy this. 

Yes, the charitable read is that constant attacking/defending leads to an overall more hardened structure. I think everyone can feel how that makes intuitive sense. 

But, I’d draw an analogy between this and Kelly betting. Everyone knows you don’t want to make repeated bets with full risk of ruin. The problem with cybersecurity and cryptocurrency is that due to the irreversible nature of transactions, you’re always in a ”risk of ruin”-like environment. If you have an automated warfare cybersecurity environment, I’d wager that your risk of ruin is actually higher, even if the ”probability of penetration per attempt” is lower. 

The fact that every possible exploit at every protocol at all times is constantly attempted… across the whole stack, at every layer… like, it’s possible that some Lindy applications like the Bitcoin baselayer would be more secure in this way. But for anything dynamic that goes through changes (e.g. Lightning, anything smart contract/upgradeable layer) the chance of an irreversible fault overall seems higher.

gm gm here we go again.

This morning somebody abused a bug in ApeStr to swap 21 apes for 21 ApeStr-owned apes.

This was a known exploit (see the SQUIGSTR exploit from ~1 year ago) but incentive to run it was never there.

The bug lies in buyTargetNFT: it forces a strategy contract to send arbitrary calldata to any target. Afterwards it checks only three things: its BAYC balance rose by exactly 1, it owns expectedId, and "cost" equals its ETH balance drop.

This was patched in later NFTStrategy releases, but affects the original 6 (PunkSTR not affected).

The attacker bought 2 BAYC to use as bait. Using a helper contract, they prep the strategy contract by selling an ape to it for 5 wei and immediately buying it back for 6 wei. That primes the contract's ethToTwap with 6 wei.

They then call buyTargetNFT and pass the calldata to transfer an ape from ApeSTR to the helper using safeTransferFrom. This in turn hands execution over to the helper (remember, safeTransferFrom is NOT safe), which transfer TWO apes back to ApeSTR to satisfy the balance check (1 out, 2 in leaves ApeSTR at +1). It also calls processTokenTwap, which converts the 6 wei, setting the cost of one of the newly deposited apes to 7 wei (6 * 120%). The helper contract buys it back in the same tx.

example flow: 
- Attacker has BAYC #1 and #2. ApeSTR has BAYC #3. 
- Attacker "sells" BAYC #1 to ApeSTR for 6 wei and sends BAYC #2 to it for free, but steals BAYC #3 in the process.
- ApeSTR relists BAYC #1 for 7 wei, which the attacker buys.
- Attacker now has BAYC #1 and BAYC #3, and ApeSTR has BAYC #2 (but doesn't even know it).

The attacker ran this for all 21 BAYC in the ApeSTR contract, resulting in them being able to claim packs for all of those BAYC. Total net proceeds: $14k.

This previously affected SQUIGSTR because of their shared contract - any art blocks NFT sent in would satisfy the balance check, allowing the attacker to drain the contract of squiggles in exchange for basically valueless art blocks NFTs.

It was known to be possible on ApeSTR as well, so I guess it was just a matter of time before we saw it happen.

The unfortunate consequence is that now, ApeSTR has 21 apes that it is completely unaware of, so they cannot be bought from the contract. And 210 attacker-owned mudwater packs were dumped into bids.

CEO Vlad Tenev emphasized that customers are entrusting more assets to the platform as Robinhood expands its financial services ecosystem, although earnings growth continues to lag revenue growth.

2. SoFi $SOFI delivered a strong Q3 2026, with revenue surging 44% YoY to $1.4B, while adjusted EPS increased 64% to $0.18 and adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% to $469.8M, highlighting accelerating growth and improving profitability. Total members climbed 35% YoY to 17.1M, reflecting continued expansion across SoFi's financial services ecosystem. Looking ahead, the company issued bullish FY2027 guidance, projecting $6.4B in revenue versus $6B expected, EPS of $0.90 versus $0.82 expected, adjusted EBITDA of $2.24B, and net income of $1.28B. CEO Anthony Noto emphasized that SoFi is attracting more members, increasing the number of products used per customer, and generating more revenue per product, reinforcing management's confidence in the company's long-term growth and profitability trajectory.

3. Chinese technology giants Alibaba $BABA, Tencent, and ByteDance are reportedly seeking long-term memory supply agreements with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, according to Korean media, as demand for AI data center infrastructure continues to accelerate. While traditional memory supply contracts typically span 3–5 years, some Chinese cloud service providers are now requesting 10-year agreements extending through 2035 to secure access to critical DDR5 and LPDDR5 memory. The unusually long contract terms highlight growing concerns over future memory availability as hyperscalers expand AI computing capacity and compete for limited supply. The development could provide Samsung and SK Hynix with greater long-term revenue visibility and reinforces the structural demand outlook for the broader memory industry, including Micron $MU.

4. Meta $META has reportedly upsized its Class A common stock offering to $25B from $22.5B, pricing the shares at $625 each as the company raises additional capital to support its massive AI infrastructure expansion. Notably, NVIDIA $NVDA is investing $3B in the offering, while AMD $AMD is committing another $1B, giving two of Meta's major AI chip suppliers direct equity exposure to one of their largest customers. The expanded offering highlights Meta's increasingly aggressive capital-raising strategy as it prepares to spend $135B–$145B on capital expenditures in 2026. The participation of NVIDIA and AMD also underscores the growing financial interconnectedness of the AI ecosystem, with semiconductor suppliers investing directly in the hyperscalers purchasing their hardware.

5. Qualcomm $QCOM and Anduril are teaming up to launch BlueChip, a new venture focused on manufacturing rugged, waterproof, American-made laptops for the U.S. military, government agencies, law enforcement, and first responders, according to the Wall Street Journal. The devices will be assembled at Anduril's Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio and powered by Qualcomm Snapdragon X processors manufactured by TSMC in Arizona. Anduril founder Palmer Luckey said approximately 90% of the planned components already come from the U.S. and allied countries, with the long-term goal of producing the entire laptop domestically, including displays and other components currently sourced overseas. The initiative prioritizes secure computing, fully traceable supply chains, and reduced dependence on foreign manufacturing for national-security applications. The first laptops are expected in 2027, with pricing estimated at roughly 20% above conventional high-end PCs.

6. President Donald Trump made two major statements, reiterating his administration's decision to replace the terms “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” with “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official executive-branch communications, following a September executive order. Separately, Trump suggested that Venezuela could eventually become the 51st U.S. state, floating the possibility of replacing its presidency with a governorship during remarks in Corpus Christi, Texas. Trump also celebrated the U.S. military intervention in Venezuela and its subsequent oil agreement, describing the operation as a historic victory and highlighting expanded American access to Venezuelan oil reserves.

The rally was primarily fueled by Barclays upgrading Tesla to Overweight and raising its price target to $450 from $370, citing improving automotive demand, accelerating energy storage growth, and a potential merger with SpaceX $SPCX that could create a premium for Tesla shareholders. Meanwhile, Tesla's robotaxi expansion continues to gain momentum, with its Texas fleet reportedly exceeding 1,050 vehicles, Cybercabs outnumbering Model Ys, and additional service areas planned, including Dallas. Investors are also responding to improving FSD adoption, strong demand for energy storage from AI data centers, and signs of stabilization in Tesla's core automotive business. 

8. Over the past 20 years, EWZ has averaged a daily return of approximately 0.04%, with a standard deviation of 2.36%, making Monday's decline an extreme statistical outlier. Under a theoretical normal distribution, a move of this magnitude would have an exceptionally small probability, illustrating just how unusual the selloff was relative to historical volatility. However, actual financial markets exhibit fat-tailed return distributions, meaning extreme declines occur more frequently than conventional statistical models predict. The plunge highlights the severity of the selling pressure in Brazilian equities and the risks associated with sudden market shocks.

9. Alphabet's $GOOGL Waymo is expanding its fully autonomous ride-hailing service by nearly 250 square miles across five existing U.S. markets over the next week, further accelerating its commercial robotaxi rollout. In Los Angeles, Waymo is extending service along the coast into the South Bay, including Torrance, while San Diego coverage will expand north to La Jolla, connecting riders to UC San Diego, the VA, and University Town Center. In Nashville, the company is expanding south to include Nashville Zoo, while Orlando will see its eastern service area nearly double alongside improved downtown coverage. The San Francisco Bay Area will also gain additional southern coverage, including a connection to Berryessa BART Station. The expansion increases Waymo's geographic reach and the number of destinations accessible to existing riders, rather than representing launches in five new cities, as Alphabet continues scaling its autonomous transportation network.

10. 11. Amazon $AMZN is reportedly working to reduce its reliance on Anthropic's AI models as the cost of operating Alexa+ continues to climb, according to Business Insider. Internal projections estimated that Alexa+ cloud computing expenses could reach approximately $1.7B in 2026, nearly triple the prior year's costs, prompting Amazon to explore routing more AI requests through its own lower-cost models and infrastructure. The company also considered delaying or scaling back Moonraker, its advanced AI agent initiative, which was projected to require more than $100M in GPU spending this year. The developments highlight the growing pressure on major technology companies to improve AI inference economics, reduce dependence on third-party model providers, and balance increasingly expensive AI capabilities with sustainable profitability.

12. U.S. stock market breadth is improving significantly, with the S&P 500 Equal-Weight Index outperforming the traditional market-cap-weighted S&P 500 by 4.0 percentage points in October, putting it on track for its second-strongest monthly relative performance since April 2009. The equal-weight index has gained 4.3% this month, compared with just 0.3% for the S&P 500, marking a sharp reversal from September, when equal-weight stocks underperformed by 4.7 percentage points, their worst relative month since March 2020. For comparison, the equal-weight index outperformed by 4.2 percentage points in April. Year-to-date, the Equal-Weight Index is up 13.4% versus 12.1% for the S&P 500, suggesting market leadership is broadening beyond the largest technology and AI companies as more sectors and individual stocks participate in the rally.

Sam Altman's one-person company prediction is coming true. Anthropic just bought one. The founder of Mithril Medicine used Claude to take a muscular dystrophy antibody treatment from concept to proof-of-principle in mice in 18 months, with just himself, Claude, and part-time consultants. The technical report is great. I will quote:

'The week opened with the handover of two cell-based assays, cell adhesion and flow cytometry, within our team, while eleven questions remained open with the assay CRO. In two sentences, one of us asked Claude to review the latest emails between the outgoing assay lead and the assay CRO and to recommend next steps for the handover, and gave it the link to the handover folder. Claude returned a bottom line after 96s and a full plan with five drafted emails after 18 min. For the full plan it read six email threads, the handover folder, two slide decks and two reports, all in the mailbox and file store to which we had given it access. Four working days later, nine of the eleven questions had an answer in writing and the other two had been left to pilot experiments. The adhesion screen was thereby set out in writing. The CRO drew the plate map to the format that our team had requested, Claude compiled the run order and the material calculation from the production data, and one of us reviewed and approved them.

On day 4, the production CRO delivered its data package, a report of 341 pages, which one of us forwarded to Claude in two sentences, with the request to review it, share observations and recommend next steps. Claude returned a bottom line after 2 min 40s and, once it had read every page, a visual synthesis of all 113 constructs after 7 min 53s. The synthesis arranged the constructs on the grid of 14 by 8 arms. Claude marked 82 constructs for screening as is, seven for additional polishing, and the 24 constructs of three laminin-binding arms to be held back from the cell-based assays on production criteria. Each of the 113 constructs thus had a proposed next step in less than 8 min.

Claude had recommended binding kinetics for all 113 con-structs, and on day 7 one of us challenged this plan. Claude defended it within 27s, arguing that affinity would show whether the three arms merit further work. One of us overruled this recommendation and set the three arms aside on production criteria. Their material remains in storage. Four minutes later, Claude had revised its memo, the working page, the run order and three unsent drafts from 113 to 89 constructs. It had also applied the ruling to three dependent steps in the unsent drafts, each flagged for our veto. The exchange took 7 min 36s from challenge to new plan, and every affected email was still an unsent draft. After the ruling, eight emails drafted by Claude went out on the same day to three CROs and a consultant.

Over the whole week, Claude drafted 17 emails, each in answer to a request from one of us, and we sent 12 of them, each after editing. With its drafts, Claude listed 41 points, such as tube fills, shipping conditions, recipients and assay settings, for which it had found no written statement of ours, so that we could confirm, change or strike each before sending. We kept some, struck others and changed one. Among the passages that we kept were proposals for controls. One draft proposed a comparison of polished and unpolished material on one sensor chip, to size the error that impurities cause in the rest of the panel. Another requested a buffer control diluted like the most dilute sample, so that any effect of the buffer appears at its largest. These proposals concerned the measurement of constructs that had already been produced, and each reached a CRO only after one of us had reviewed and approved it.
